title: Progressive-slice-batcher: Tail-padding reduction via slice-aware slot splitting
author: Asha Kumar
description:
Motivation: long-tail sequence length variance causes substantial padding waste in continuous batching. Existing bucketing reduces some padding but struggles with heavy-tailed requests and mixed workloads. This PR implements a progressive slice batcher that slices long requests into bounded 'slices' that can be packed alongside short sequences, plus a slice-aware slot-splitting allocator and KV-prefetch alignment to avoid cache thrashing.

What this changes: single-string summary of sections below. Algorithm: introduce slice-aware scoring that computes an amortized pad-cost per-slot and a kernel-fit score that prefers packing slices into underfilled slots when pad-cost reduction outweighs the extra scheduling overhead. Very long sequences are split into contiguous slices of configurable target length (SLICE_TARGET) and an allowed remainder; slices carry metadata so KV cache prefetch can align slice boundaries with KV segments to reduce prefill misses. A new "progressive split" policy optionally splits only when expected padded token savings exceed a threshold (PAD_SAVINGS_THRESHOLD).

Runtime integration: integrates with continuous-batcher by adding a BatchComposer stage that emits slice-units; the SlotAllocator was extended to accept slice affinity and to do slot-splitting heuristics that maintain order constraints for single-request slices. KV path: added a prefill alignment pass that groups slice prefetches by KV key-range so that adjacent slices reuse warm KV segments and reduce duplicate prefill costs.

Configuration knobs (defaults included): SLICE_TARGET=128, SLICE_MAX=512, PAD_COST_WEIGHT=1.6, PAD_SAVINGS_THRESHOLD=0.12, SLOT_MERGE_HORIZON_MS=5. These live in runtime/config/batching.toml and are hot-reloadable in Dedicated/Private modes.

Benchmarks: measured on rtx-pool (4xA100) with our synthetic heavy-tail trace (generated from production seqlen histogram): compared to current main: - P95 token latency reduced by 18% on mixed-heavy-tail workload; - average tokens/sec per-GPU increased by 12% for batcher-bound workloads; - end-to-end request latency for long requests increased tail by ~2% due to splitting overhead but overall client-visible median latency improved. Microbenchmarks: KV-prefetch hit-rate improved from 72% to 88% on slice-composed workloads.

Tests & safety: added unit/CI tests for slice boundary correctness, order preservation for single-request slices, and KV-prefetch alignment; added perf regression harness test that runs a 30s canary trace. Canary rollout: start with 10% traffic for 72 hours, monitor P95 latency, error-rate, and KV-prefill CPU; automatic rollback if P95 degrades >5% or error-rate increases >0.5% relative to baseline.

Related: references ENG-12891 (batching heuristics spike) and ENG-12952 (kv-prefetch tuning). Links: Linear tasks and internal perf dashboards included in commit notes.

Checklist: [x] design doc updated, [x] unit tests, [x] perf tests, [x] docs page, [x] canary plan included.

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of ordering guarantees and on potential KV prefill thundering; I added a lightweight leaky token bucket to throttle concurrent slice-prefetches as a safety valve.

review_comments: Marco Reyes: This looks promising — please clarify ordering semantics when a single request is sliced across multiple slots. Will slices be interleaved with other requests?

Author (Asha Kumar): Slices preserve in-request ordering via a per-request sequence token. The SlotAllocator will mark slices as dependent and only allow interleaving when the request's downstream consumer can reassemble; if not, the allocator keeps slices colocated. Added tests to demonstrate behavior.
Hannah Yeo: Concern: KV-prefetch might create duplicate work for adjacent slices; can we coalesce prefetches across slot boundaries?
Author: Implemented prefetch alignment pass that groups slice prefetches by KV segment and a small coalescer with a 2-slot lookahead. Throttle added to avoid thundering herd.
Devon Patel: CI flake in test_slice_batching on macOS runner; please ensure test isolation for RNG seeds and timing stubs.
Author: Fixed by using deterministic seeds and replacing a timing-dependent assertion with a normalized window check (commit c9e1d02).
Marco Reyes: Approved after the deterministic test fix and benchmark numbers attached to the PR description.
CI Bot: All checks passed (unit, lints, perf-harness).

release_notes: Introduce a progressiveSlice batcher that slices very long sequences to reduce padding waste and improve GPU utilization. Includes KV-prefetch alignment and slot-splitting heuristics. Opt-in via SLICE_TARGET in batching config; canary rollout recommended.
notes: This PR aims to reduce padding amortized cost on heavy-tail workloads. Operators should monitor KV-prefetch CPU and P95 latency during canary. Default settings are conservative; enable aggressive splitting only after canary verification.
